To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recurrent neural network with the combination of features (lane centering, steering wheel angle and lateral velocity) is the most accurate machine learning technique in terms of lane change prediction.

the recurrent neural network outperformed both other approaches and that the feature combination of the lateral deviation of the ego-vehicle, the lateral deviation of a lead vehicle and the relative velocity between the vehicles was the most appropriate for the prediction of lane changes in a traffic simulation environment.

the combination of a support vector machine and a combination of features including lane change intentions, the position of the car in the lane and the position of the vehicle ahead is the best approach to predict lane change behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of human lane change behavior in a traffic simulation.
a first approach to the application of machine learning techniques in autonomous driving.
the question, if and how machine learning techniques can be used in order to predict the behavior of humans in the context of autonomous driving.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all three methods are suitable to predict lane changes.
the recurrent neural network is the most promising approach for the prediction of human driving behavior.
the best performing machine learning technique depends heavily on the feature set used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to predict lane change behavior with a mean accuracy of 85.4 %.

the combination of the feature combination “lane center, speed and steering wheel angle” in combination with the support vector machine with radial basis function kernel is the most appropriate approach to predict lane changes.
the best performance was achieved by the recurrent neural network with a feature set containing 7 different features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of a recurrent neural network with the features of the vehicle's speed and the vehicle's lateral position in the lane performs best.
the best performing system uses a combination of the most relevant features and a recurrent neural network.
machine learning is an appropriate approach to model the lane change behavior of humans in traffic.
